subject: Q4 staffing triage — freeze exceptions and backfill prioritization
messages:
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: michael_grant@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 staffing triage — freeze exceptions and backfill prioritization

Team,

As part of QBR prep and the updated budget guardrails, we need to lock down which open reqs proceed this quarter and which are frozen. I pulled together a short summary (attached) of the seven active reqs owned by Platform, DX, and Growth. High level asks:

- Can each of you confirm priority (1/2/3) on the listed reqs by EOD Monday?
- Approve up to two immediate backfills (critical ops / SRE) if rationale holds.
- Sign off on a temporary freeze for non-customer-facing hires unless we identify a compelling revenue tie.

Notes from my side: we should prioritize SRE backfill (req_541) and one senior frontend IC to unblock product launches. Growth analyst can wait until after the QBR unless we secure a pilot budget.

Attachments: Q4_headcount_request_summary.xlsx; req_541_frontend_backfill.docx

Thanks — I'd like to present a recommended ask to the Execs on Tuesday's QBR prep call.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

--

(attachment stub: Q4_headcount_request_summary.xlsx - spreadsheet summarizing reqs, owners, requested start date)

Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 staffing triage — freeze exceptions and backfill prioritization

Aditya —

Quick take from Product / Eng:
- req_541 (SRE backfill) = Priority 1. We cannot hit the Q4 throughput targets without this headcount.
- req_548 (senior frontend) = Priority 2. Launch is important, but we have a short-term contractor option (BrightHire) for up to 8 weeks.
- req_553 (growth analyst) = Priority 3 — can be paused.

If Finance is strict on headcount, approve req_541 immediately and put req_548 on a 30-day decision window (contractor in place if needed).

On the contract/market side, I've asked ops@brighthire.com for availability and rough rate — they responded they can spin someone up in ~2 weeks.

-Michael
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi all,

HR notes and timeline:
- Budget: We have 1.6 FTEs available under the current hiring envelope if Headcount Committee approves exceptions. Any additional hires will require offset or reallocation.
- req_541 (SRE) — clearance: green. Standard background + offer timeline = 10–14 business days once approved.
- req_548 (frontend) — contractor is feasible; but converting a contractor later will need an additional spot. Recommend marking as "conditional hire" (approve contractor now, convert later pending QBR outcome).
- req_560 (comms) — strongly recommend hold/freeze (not customer-critical).

I've uploaded a short tracker to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-Staffing-2026 (see sheet "Commitments") and created JIRA SUP-1984 to track approval flow.

If you want, TalentOps can draft exception language for the Exec packet — copying them here.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the fast turnarounds. Consolidating decisions for the QBR packet:

- Approve req_541 (SRE backfill) as Priority 1 — request Exec sign-off for immediate offer (HR timeline fits).
- Approve contractor engagement for req_548 (senior frontend) as interim (BrightHire). Do not use a headcount slot yet — mark conditional.
- Freeze req_560 (comms) and req_553 (growth analyst) until post-QBR review.

Mina — please proceed with offer paperwork for req_541 and add the conditional contractor engagement for req_548 in the tracker. Grace — can you confirm for the Exec packet that two exceptions (one backfill + one contractor) are acceptable from a leadership perspective?

I'll include this recommendation in the QBR prep doc and bring these points up during the leadership readout.

-Aditya
Director, Product Operations
